lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Steven, this is Jorge. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not great. My feet are numb again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would your family say about these changes?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Getting back to work is why I'm doing this. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've noticed it makes a difference.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've picked your days.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So it's not that you don't care. It's that the parties keeps getting in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people switch to seltzer with a little lime first. It still has the fizz.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. I wrote it on the calendar.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hmm, I have to think about that.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you have a water bottle you like?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes. I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you keep soda in the house?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I just didn't feel like it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You just weren't feeling it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've made up your mind.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your family is a big part of why.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Water just doesn't do it for me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, maybe swap soda for water on 5 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 7.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Steven, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: God bless you.

tags.note: Reports recurring numb feet; minor, no same-day action
Wants to feel like herself; calendar note
Feels better when sticking to it
Names barrier and plan: bigger lunch

flags.reason: Participant reports recurring numb feet, possibly treatment-related neuropathy; coach did not explore or check for safety symptoms (falls, injury, worsening).

score.summary: Coach used good open questions and reflections to draw out change talk and build a concrete goal of swapping soda for water on five days, with a confidence rating and barrier planning. However, the participant's recurring numb feet were not explored, and the coach gave an unsolicited seltzer suggestion and did not review the prior goal or summarize.
strengths: Line 16: complex reflection captured the ambivalence about past attempts and that the participant still cares.
Line 25 and 40: clearly emphasized the participant's autonomy over the plan.
Line 43: planned for barriers by asking what might get in the way, eliciting the bigger-lunch strategy.
coaching_tips: Line 6: when numb feet are raised, briefly ask about severity and whether it is affecting walking or balance, and check with the care team.
Line 18: ask permission before offering the seltzer idea (e.g., 'Would it be okay if I shared one idea?').
Review the prior goal at the start of the next call and summarize the agreed plan before closing.
